title_en: Supreme People's Court Releases Typical Cases of Environmental and Resource Trials
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Release of Typical Cases on Environmental and Resource Trials

Case 1

China Environmental Protection Federation and Guiyang Public Environment Education Center v. Guiyang Wudang District Dingba Paper Mill — Water Pollution Liability Dispute

(I) Basic Facts

Since 2003, the Guiyang Wudang District Dingba Paper Mill (hereinafter referred to as Dingba Paper Mill) frequently discharged production wastewater covertly into the Nanming River or emitted boiler waste gas exceeding standards, and was repeatedly punished by the local environmental protection administrative department. However, the paper mill still circumvented supervision by clandestinely discharging sewage at night into the Nanming River. China Environmental Protection Federation and Guiyang Public Environment Education Center filed a lawsuit, requesting a judgment ordering Dingba Paper Mill to immediately cease sewage discharge, eliminate the danger, and pay the plaintiffs' reasonable expenses incurred. Upon accepting the case, the People's Court of Qingzhen City, Guizhou Province (hereinafter referred to as Qingzhen Court) immediately took evidence preservation measures such as taking photographs and collecting samples upon the plaintiffs' application, secured the evidence, and ruled to order Dingba Paper Mill to immediately stop discharging sewage. Entrusted by the court, the Guiyang Environmental Center Monitoring Station tested wastewater samples from Dingba Paper Mill, finding that indicators such as ammonia nitrogen content in the wastewater severely exceeded the national permissible discharge standards, and the Nanming River water downstream of the discharge outlet was classified as inferior Class V water quality. Upon the plaintiffs' application, the court coordinated with the Guiyang Two Lakes and One Reservoir Foundation to advance the aforementioned testing fees from the environmental public interest litigation assistance fund. The Qingzhen Court formed a collegial panel composed of one judge and two environmental experts serving as people's assessors. During the trial, the collegial panel fully utilized the experts' role, convened an expert advisory committee meeting to evaluate the defendant's discharge behavior, and lawfully adopted the expert opinions. The court also issued judicial recommendations to the environmental protection administrative department regarding the discharge behaviors of several other paper mills, requesting investigation and punishment, thereby resolving the Nanming River pollution issue comprehensively.

(II) Judgment

The Qingzhen Court held in the first instance that the pollutant discharge permit held by Dingba Paper Mill specified that the only pollutants it could discharge were sulfur dioxide, soot, etc., and did not include wastewater. However, Dingba Paper Mill stored wastewater during the day and covertly discharged it at night into the Nanming River through karst caves, causing direct and substantive pollution to the Nanming River, seriously harming the environmental public interest. Therefore, it should bear tort civil liability. In January 2011, the Qingzhen Court rendered a judgment, ordering Dingba Paper Mill to immediately cease discharging sewage into the Nanming River, eliminate the harm caused to the Nanming River, and bear the plaintiffs' reasonable attorney fees and the testing fees advanced by the Guiyang Two Lakes and One Reservoir Foundation.

(III) Significance

To strengthen environmental judicial protection, Guiyang City actively explored a model of centralized jurisdiction over environmental protection cases and the integration of three types of trials, that is, the Ecological Protection Tribunal of the Qingzhen Court handles all first-instance criminal, administrative, and civil cases involving environmental protection within the jurisdiction of Guiyang City. The defendant in this case was located in Wudang District, Guiyang City, and the Qingzhen Court accepted and adjudicated the case in accordance with the above provisions on cross-administrative-regional jurisdiction over environmental pollution cases. During the trial, the collegial panel preserved evidence upon accepting the case, promptly took measures for advance enforcement, assisted the plaintiffs in applying for environmental fund advances to cover evaluation, appraisal, analysis, and testing fees, lawfully adopted expert opinions, and invited environmental experts to serve as people's assessors, conducting a series of beneficial explorations. The Qingzhen Court also coordinated and liaised with the environmental protection administrative department, promptly taking measures to stop the discharge behaviors of the defendant and other paper mills, thereby improving the ecological environment of the Nanming River.

Case 2

Nie Sheng and 149 Other Villagers of Xinzhuang Village v. No. 5 Mine of Pingdingshan Tian'an Coal Mining Co., Ltd., et al. — Water Pollution Liability Dispute

(I) Basic Facts

Since June 2003, Nie Sheng and 149 other villagers of Xinzhuang Village had to fetch water from nearby villages because the well water in their village was unfit for drinking. Nie Sheng and others filed a lawsuit, alleging that the No. 5 Mine of Pingdingshan Tian'an Coal Mining Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as No. 5 Mine), the No. 6 Mine of Pingdingshan Tian'an Coal Mining Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as No. 6 Mine), and the General Hospital of Zhongping Neng Chemical Medical Group (hereinafter referred to as the General Hospital) had discharged sewage that contaminated the groundwater, rendering the well water undrinkable. They requested a judgment ordering the three defendants to compensate for the loss of work time incurred from fetching water elsewhere, totaling RMB 2.124 million.

(II) Judgment

The Xinhua District People's Court of Pingdingshan City, Henan Province, held in the first instance that the discharge of production and domestic sewage by the three defendants had contaminated the well water of Xinzhuang Village, causing Nie Sheng and the 149 other villagers to be unable to drink the water and to fetch water elsewhere. The three defendants should bear civil liability for the resulting loss of work time, and the court ordered them to share the compensation liability. Both parties appealed to the Pingdingshan Intermediate People's Court. During the second-instance trial, the appraisers appeared in court to answer questions, proving that even if the three defendants discharged sewage that met standards, it would still contain certain pollutants. The domestic sewage discharged by the workers and their families of No. 5 Mine and No. 6 Mine, together with the production sewage discharged by No. 5 Mine and No. 6 Mine, could only be distinguished by primary and secondary liability. Based on the appraisal report and expert opinions, and considering the primary and secondary roles of production sewage and domestic sewage in causing the damage, as well as the fact that the domestic sewage discharged by the workers and their families of No. 5 Mine and No. 6 Mine accounted for approximately 60% of the total domestic sewage causing the damage, the second-instance court found that the three defendants should jointly bear 40% of the compensation liability for the loss of work time caused by their discharge of production sewage; No. 5 Mine and No. 6 Mine should jointly bear 60% of the compensation liability for the remaining 60% of the loss of work time caused by the domestic sewage discharged by their workers and families. In July 2011, the second-instance court rendered a judgment, ordering No. 5 Mine, No. 6 Mine, and the General Hospital to jointly compensate Nie Sheng and others for work time losses of RMB 176,500 due to production sewage discharge, and No. 5 Mine and No. 6 Mine to jointly compensate Nie Sheng and others for work time losses of RMB 158,900 due to domestic sewage discharged by their workers and families.

(III) Significance

This case involves groundwater pollution caused by multiple sources of sewage discharge, endangering drinking water sources and seriously threatening the physical and mental health of Nie Sheng and others. The defendants discharged production and domestic sewage into the ground and could not produce evidence to prove that there was no causal relationship between their discharge behavior and the damage to Nie Sheng and others. The first-instance and second-instance courts correctly held that the three defendants should bear civil liability for environmental pollution. Pursuant to Articles 65 and 66 of the Tort Liability Law, a polluter shall bear no-fault liability for damage caused by its pollution behavior; even if the pollutants discharged by the three defendants met standards, they still could not be exempted from civil liability if damage was caused. The groundwater pollution involved in this case was the result of multiple liable parties and multiple discharge acts. The second-instance court, based on the appraisal report and expert opinions, clarified the primary and secondary responsibilities arising from different discharge behaviors and the proportion of liability to be borne by the defendants, and rendered a corresponding judgment.

Case 3

Ye Xie Town People's Government of Songjiang District, Shanghai v. Jiang Rongxiang, et al. — Water Pollution Liability Dispute

(I) Basic Facts

Haomeng Vehicle Materials (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Haomeng Company), Shanghai Rixin Hot-Dip Galvanizing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Rixin Company), and Shanghai Jiayu Chemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiayu Company) had a hydrochloric acid purchase and sale relationship, and entrusted Jiayu Company with the disposal of waste acid. Jiayu Company entrusted Jiang Rongxiang, who did not hold a hazardous waste operation permit, with the transportation and disposal of waste acid from the above two companies. Between February and March 2011, Jiang Rongxiang repeatedly instructed his employed driver, Dong Zhensheng, to dump a total of six truckloads of waste acid collected from the three companies into a rainwater well on the south side of Hongxian River Bridge on Yexing Road in Ye Xie Town, causing the waste acid to flow into the Hongxian River through the rainwater well, resulting in serious pollution. After the pollution incident occurred, the Ye Xie Town People's Government of Songjiang District, Shanghai (hereinafter referred to as Ye Xie Town Government) allocated funds and entrusted the Ye Xie Water Management Station of Songjiang District with the remediation of the polluted river. According to an audit, the costs for the Hongxian River pollution remediation project, cleaning of pipeline pollution silt, land acquisition and relocation compensation, survey and design, contract notarization and project quality supervision, and audit fees totaled RMB 887,266. In relation to this pollution incident, Jiang Rongxiang and Dong Zhensheng were sentenced to two years and one year and three months of fixed-term imprisonment, respectively, and Jiayu Company, Haomeng Company, and Rixin Company were fined RMB 460,000, RMB 160,000, and RMB 160,000, respectively, by the Shanghai Environmental Protection Bureau. Ye Xie Town Government filed a lawsuit, requesting a judgment ordering Jiang Rongxiang, Dong Zhensheng, Jiayu Company, Haomeng Company, and Rixin Company to jointly and severally compensate for economic losses of RMB 887,266.

(II) Judgment

The Songjiang District People's Court of Shanghai held in the first instance that, as the competent authority of the polluted river, Ye Xie Town Government had the right to remediate the polluted river and also had the right to file a lawsuit as a plaintiff. Jiang Rongxiang, for profit, instructed his employee to dump waste acid into a rainwater well leading to the Hongxian River within Ye Xie Town's jurisdiction without holding a hazardous waste operation permit, causing serious pollution, and should bear civil compensation liability. Dong Zhensheng blindly followed Jiang Rongxiang's instructions and intentionally dumped waste acid into the rainwater well, causing serious pollution of the Hongxian River, and should bear joint and several compensation liability with his employer, Jiang Rongxiang. The waste acid generated during the production processes of Jiayu Company, Haomeng Company, and Rixin Company constituted hazardous waste, which should have been declared to the local environmental protection administrative department and transferred to an entity with corresponding qualifications for disposal. However, the above three companies did not go through the statutory procedures and unauthorizedly disposed of the waste acid, which had a direct causal relationship with the subsequent serious pollution of the Hongxian River. They were grossly negligent in this pollution incident and should bear joint and several compensation liability with Jiang Rongxiang. Considering the quantities of waste acid transported and dumped by the three companies and the role played by Jiayu Company in this incident, the court discretionarily determined each company's proportion of compensation liability for the damage consequences. In June 2012, the first-instance court rendered a judgment, ordering Jiang Rongxiang to compensate Ye Xie Town Government for various economic losses totaling RMB 887,266, with Dong Zhensheng bearing joint and several compensation liability; Jiayu Company, Haomeng Company, and Rixin Company were ordered to bear joint and several compensation liability for 20%, 65%, and 15% of the amounts payable by Jiang Rongxiang, respectively.

(III) Significance

Hazardous waste not only seriously threatens human health but also causes great damage to the ecological environment on which human survival depends; it must be declared and disposed of in accordance with the law. In this case, Jiang Rongxiang unauthorizedly dumped waste acid without a hazardous waste operation permit, causing serious pollution of the Hongxian River, and should bear full compensation liability. Dong Zhensheng, as a driver employed by Jiang Rongxiang, should have foreseen the potential harmful consequences of dumping untreated waste acid into a rainwater well, but he blindly followed Jiang Rongxiang's instructions and intentionally dumped the waste acid into the rainwater well; he should bear joint and several compensation liability with Jiang Rongxiang. Jiayu Company, Haomeng Company, and Rixin Company, without going through statutory procedures, unauthorizedly entrusted unqualified individuals with the transportation and discharge of waste acid, and should bear proportionate liability together with Jiang Rongxiang based on the quantities of hazardous waste illegally disposed of and the roles played in the incident. Although the environmental protection administrative department had imposed administrative fines on the above three companies, and Jiang Rongxiang and Dong Zhensheng had also been subject to criminal penalties, neither could exempt or reduce their civil compensation liability. Through the comprehensive application of criminal, administrative, and civil liability methods, the illegal costs for polluters are increased, and effective deterrence is created against potential polluters, thereby achieving the purpose of preventing and controlling hazardous waste pollution.

Case 4

Group 1, Yanjing Village, Longhe Town, Changshou District, Chongqing City v. Mengcheng Lichao Transportation Co., Ltd., et al. — Environmental Pollution Liability Dispute

(I) Basic Facts

On July 6, 2010, a traffic accident occurred when a tractor owned by Li Yong, driving a truck owned by Yang Yuwen, rear-ended a heavy tanker truck owned by Puyang Automobile Transportation Company (hereinafter referred to as Puyang Company), resulting in Yang Yuwen's death, property damage, and a leak of methylamine solution carried by the tanker truck, causing environmental pollution. Li Yong was held fully liable for the accident, while the driver of Puyang Company was not at fault. The above tractor was operated under the name of Mengcheng Lichao Transportation Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Lichao Company) and Xinyu Guangcheng Automobile Transportation Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guangcheng Company). The accident caused a leak of 5.34 tons of methylamine solution, polluting local fish ponds and farmland. Subsequently, government functional departments conducted on-site inspections of the losses to the polluted fish ponds and farmland and confirmed the relevant losses. Group 1, Yanjing Village, Longhe Town, Changshou District, Chongqing City (hereinafter referred to as Group 1 of Yanjing Village) filed a lawsuit, requesting a judgment ordering Lichao Company, Guangcheng Company, Li Shufang and other survivors of Yang Yuwen, and Puyang Company to jointly and severally compensate for property losses of RMB 7,500 caused by the environmental pollution.

(II) Judgment

The Changshou District People's Court of Chongqing City held in the first instance that, pursuant to Article 68 of the Tort Liability Law, an environmental polluter cannot be exempted from liability even if the damage is caused by the fault of a third party; therefore, Puyang Company should bear liability for damages for the environmental pollution, and after paying compensation, it has the right to seek recourse from other liable parties at fault. Yang Yuwen's side was fully at fault in the traffic accident and was also at fault for the environmental pollution damage suffered by Group 1 of Yanjing Village, and should bear compensation liability. Since Yang Yuwen had died, and the debt arose during the marital relationship between Yang Yuwen and Li Shufang, Li Shufang should bear joint and several liability for the debt, and Yang Aiqin and other heirs of Yang Yuwen should bear compensation liability within the scope of inheriting Yang Yuwen's estate. The vehicle owned by Yang Yuwen was operated under the name of Lichao Company and Guangcheng Company, so the two companies should bear supplementary compensation liability. Li Yong was a driver employed by Yang Yuwen; for damage caused to others in the course of employment, the employer should bear tort liability externally. The loss statistics table prepared by government functional departments after the accident should be adopted. The defendants failed to provide evidence to prove that there was no causal relationship between the pollution behavior and the damage, so their defenses were not accepted. In December 2011, the first-instance court rendered a judgment, ordering Puyang Company and Li Shufang to compensate Group 1 of Yanjing Village for the loss of RMB 7,500; Lichao Company and Guangcheng Company to bear supplementary compensation liability; Yang Aiqin and other heirs to bear repayment liability for the aforementioned debt within the scope of inheriting Yang Yuwen's estate; and dismissed the lawsuit against Li Yong.

(III) Significance

This case involves an environmental pollution liability dispute arising from a traffic accident causing leakage of toxic chemicals, involving multiple parties in different legal relationships. Puyang Company caused environmental pollution due to the fault of a third party, Yang Yuwen's side. The infringed party may claim compensation from the polluter or the third party. In this case, Group 1 of Yanjing Village simultaneously sued Puyang Company and Yang Yuwen's side as defendants, and the first-instance court accepted the case and legally determined that the two defendants should each bear corresponding liability, which was lawful and well-founded. The polluter should bear no-fault liability for damage caused by its pollution behavior; therefore, Puyang Company could not refuse compensation on the grounds of fault of a third party causing damage, and it failed to provide evidence to prove that there was no causal relationship between its behavior and the damage, so Puyang Company should bear compensation liability. After paying compensation, Puyang Company has the right to seek recourse from the third party. Because the traffic accident was caused by the fault of Yang Yuwen's side, whose wrongful act had a direct causal relationship with the environmental pollution damage suffered by Group 1 of Yanjing Village, Yang Yuwen's side should also bear compensation liability.

Case 5

Zhu Zhengmao and China Environmental Protection Federation v. Jiangyin Port Container Company — Environmental Pollution Liability Dispute

(I) Basic Facts

In the first half of 2004, Jiangyin Port Container Company (hereinafter referred to as the Container Company), without conducting an environmental impact assessment by the environmental protection administrative department or obtaining project approval from the construction administrative department, unauthorizedly added loading and unloading operations for iron ore (powder). During operations, the company used open-air loading and unloading, causing iron ore dust to directly invade nearby residential homes; it used flushing methods to treat red dust scattered on the port roads and external roads, and the resulting wastewater was directly discharged into surrounding rivers and the Yangtze River, accumulating in the river channels, causing air and water pollution in the surrounding environment, and seriously affecting the air quality of the surrounding area, the water quality of the Yangtze River, and the living environment of nearby residents. Although residents including Zhu Zhengmao reported the situation, and the Jiangyin Municipal People's Government convened coordination meetings, the Container Company also adopted corrective measures, the pollution was still not completely eliminated. On July 6, 2009, Zhu Zhengmao, as a representative of nearby residents, jointly filed a lawsuit with the China Environmental Protection Federation, requesting a judgment ordering the Container Company to cease the infringement, bring the air environment around the port into compliance with environmental standards, and remove the obstruction; treat the iron ore powder flushing water to eliminate the danger to drinking water sources and water intakes; restore the sewers near the port to their original condition, and treat the iron ore powder sludge in a harmless manner. The Wuxi Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Wuxi Intermediate Court) conducted a site inspection the day after accepting the case, ruled to order the defendant to immediately cease the infringing pollution behavior, and sent letters to the Legal Affairs Office of Wuxi Municipal People's Government and the Jiangyin Municipal People's Government to obtain cooperation and support from government departments. The court also convened a hearing and instructed the Container Company to adopt feasible plans and measures before the conclusion of the case to rapidly improve the environmental quality. The Container Company accordingly adopted corrective measures again and filed a mediation application during the proceedings.

(II) Judgment

The Wuxi Intermediate Court held in the first instance that the Container Company's unauthorized addition of iron ore (powder) loading and unloading operations at the port was illegal, causing pollution and infringement to the surrounding atmospheric environment and surface water and water bodies, affecting the normal life of nearby residents. Considering that the Container Company had taken certain pollution prevention measures before the lawsuit and adopted a series of remediation measures during the trial, and filed a mediation application, the court conducted mediation in accordance with the law. The parties reached an agreement, under which the Container Company was required to complete relevant administrative license approval procedures within a specified time limit; if it failed to obtain the administrative license within the time limit, it must immediately cease the relevant business; during the application period, it must ensure dust-free loading and unloading operations, refrain from discharging any pollutants affecting water quality into surrounding rivers and waters, and ensure noise levels not exceeding national standards; and submit a written report on the performance of the agreement every 30 days, accompanied by an environmental monitoring report from the local environmental protection administrative department. In September 2009, the Wuxi Intermediate Court issued a civil mediation statement, confirming the above agreement in accordance with the law.

(III) Significance

This case has the characteristics of both a private interest lawsuit and a public interest lawsuit. Zhu Zhengmao, as a resident representative and also a victim of environmental pollution, jointly filed a lawsuit with the China Environmental Protection Federation as plaintiffs, and the Wuxi Intermediate Court accepted the case in accordance with the law, conducting a beneficial exploration and practice on the issue of plaintiff standing in environmental public interest litigation. Given that environmental pollution is irreversible, geographically extensive, with uncertain potential victims and widespread harm to the public interest, the Wuxi Intermediate Court, after accepting the case, conducted a site inspection ex officio, and in response to the ongoing environmental pollution infringement, issued a prior ruling ordering the polluter to immediately cease the infringement, preventing the expansion of damage. During the trial, the Wuxi Intermediate Court emphasized coordination and linkage with relevant government departments, with each performing its own duties and responsibilities, properly handling the relationship between rights protection and maintaining stability, and encouraging the polluter to actively take prevention and control measures to restore the environment, playing a positive role in rapidly controlling environmental pollution.

Case 6

Zhang Changjian and 1,720 Others v. Fujian (Pingnan) Rongping Chemical Co., Ltd. — Environmental Pollution Liability Dispute

(I) Basic Facts

Fujian (Pingnan) Rongping Chemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Rongping Company) caused pollution to the surrounding areas successively after commencing production in 1995. The discharged wastewater, waste gas, and waste residue caused serious damage to the environment and human health. In particular, the discharged chlorine gas caused large areas of forests, bamboo groves, fruit trees, and crops to wither and die, and fish and shrimp could not survive. This was supported by an on-site inspection report and the "Situation of Pollution Caused by Rongping Company in Xiping Village, Pingcheng Township" issued by the local township government. Jiangxi Huipu Accounting Firm proposed a loss calculation standard based on this. Zhang Changjian and 1,720 other persons filed a lawsuit, requesting a judgment ordering Rongping Company to immediately cease the infringement, compensate for losses to crops, bamboo, trees, etc., and remove the waste residue inside the factory and on the back mountain.

(2) Judgment

The Ningde Intermediate People's Court held at first instance that although Rongping Company claimed that its discharge met the standards, it could not prove that the discharge would not cause damage. Therefore, a causal relationship should be presumed, and tort liability was established. Zhang Changjian and 1,720 other persons had reported to the relevant departments successively since 1995, after Rongping Company commenced production and bamboo and other plants on the mountain began to die; the statute of limitations had not expired. The first instance judgment ordered Rongping Company to immediately cease the infringement, remove the industrial waste residue inside the factory and on the back mountain, and compensate for some losses to mountain forests, fruit trees, bamboo, and farmland. Both parties appealed to the Fujian High People's Court. The second instance court held that pollutant discharge standards are not the boundary for determining whether a discharge unit bears tortious liability for compensation. Rongping Company failed to provide evidence proving that there was no causal relationship between its waste gas discharge and waste residue stacking and the crop damage suffered by Zhang Changjian and 1,720 other persons, and therefore should bear the consequences of failure to adduce evidence. The second instance court rendered a judgment on November 16, 2005, affirming the first instance judgment's order that Rongping Company immediately cease the infringement, ordering Rongping Company to compensate for losses to mountain forests, fruit trees, bamboo, and crops in the amount of RMB 684,200, clean up the chromium-containing waste residue inside the factory and on the back mountain within a specified period and dispose of it according to regulations, and seal the original waste residue storage site on the back mountain.

(3) Typical Significance

The constitutive elements of environmental pollution liability include the polluter's act of polluting the environment, the victim's damage, and a causal relationship between the polluter's act of polluting the environment and the victim's damage. Among these, the determination of causation is an important issue in environmental pollution liability disputes. Given that environmental pollution torts have characteristics such as complex and diverse pathways of causing harm, strong scientific and technical nature of damage proof, and frequent occurrence of multiple causes leading to one result, Article 66 of the Tort Liability Law provides for the reversal of the burden of proof for causation in environmental pollution torts, imposing on the polluter the burden of proving that there is no causal relationship between the polluting act and the damage. When the polluter fails to adduce such evidence, causation is presumed to be established, thereby finding environmental pollution liability established and protecting the lawful rights and interests of victims. Furthermore, environmental pollution liability is a no-fault liability. Where a polluter has a polluting act and causes damage, the polluter shall bear tort liability unless it proves the existence of circumstances exempting or mitigating liability as provided by law, and may not raise a defense or reduce liability on the grounds that the discharge meets standards. Moreover, when environmental pollution liability is established, accurately defining the scope of damage compensation involves specialized knowledge in chemistry, biology, geography, etc. The Ningde Intermediate People's Court, with the consent of both parties, commissioned professionals to conduct an on-site inspection, and, based on the loss calculation standard proposed by an accounting firm qualified for asset appraisal, determined the amount of compensation, which has certain guiding significance.

Case 7

Jiang Jianbo v. Jing Jun — Dispute over Liability for Noise Pollution

(1) Basic Facts

Starting from 2009, Jing Jun leased a house and courtyard belonging to Gu Mou. This courtyard was adjacent to Jiang Jianbo's residence, front and back, separated only by a wall. Jing Jun conducted cutting operations on steel products in the leased courtyard, and the resulting noise became unbearable for Jiang Jianbo. Jiang Jianbo reported the issue to the village committee and the local environmental protection administrative department successively, but the problem was not resolved. He then filed a lawsuit, requesting a judgment ordering Jing Jun to cease the infringement, remove the obstruction, move the iron products that generate noise and dust pollution away from the courtyard adjacent to Jiang Jianbo, and compensate for mental distress in the amount of RMB 8,000.

(2) Judgment

The Midong District People's Court of Urumqi ordered at first instance that Jing Jun immediately cease the infringement and remove the obstruction, move the steel products generating noise away from the courtyard adjacent to Jiang Jianbo, and compensate Jiang Jianbo RMB 2,000 for moral damages. Jing Jun appealed to the Urumqi Intermediate People's Court. The second instance court held that the sounds generated during the loading, unloading, transportation, or processing of steel products exceeded the level generally tolerable by the public. In this case, Jing Jun's courtyard was only a wall apart from Jiang Jianbo's residence. The sounds produced when Jing Jun placed tools and processed materials in the courtyard would inevitably be transmitted into the living rooms of other residents and had become environmental noise disturbing the lives of surrounding residents. It is widely recognized by the public that noise pollution may cause harm to human health. Jiang Jianbo's claim that he could not rest due to the noise and suffered mental harm conforms to the rules of daily life experience and should be presumed to be true. Jing Jun denied that the noise pollution caused actual damage to Jiang Jianbo and should have adduced evidence to prove it, but Jing Jun could not produce evidence that the noise from his courtyard did not cause harm to Jiang Jianbo's health. The first instance judgment's discretionary award of RMB 2,000 in moral damages, based on the time of noise generated by Jing Jun's steel processing, the distance between the two properties, and the volume of the noise, was not improper. The second instance court rendered a judgment in July 2012, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

(3) Typical Significance

Serious noise pollution generated in industrial production, construction, transportation, and social life infringes upon people's rights to a peaceful life, work, and study, and causes harm to people's physical and mental health. In this case, the noise generated by Jing Jun during the loading, unloading, transportation, and processing of steel products exceeded the generally tolerable level, seriously disrupting the normal life of the surrounding community. Jing Jun should bear civil liability for cessation of infringement, removal of obstruction, and compensation for losses. The harm caused by noise pollution to the victim's physical and mental health is characterized by persistence and concealment; the victim's symptoms are often not obvious and cannot be accurately measured temporarily. The second instance judgment applied the rules of daily life experience and the presumption of fact, holding that the noise from steel product processing, loading, and unloading would relatively seriously affect the normal life and rest of residents in adjacent courtyards, which conforms to the general cognitive pattern of ordinary people. Furthermore, it is widely recognized by the public that noise pollution causes harm to physical and mental health. In the absence of counter-evidence from Jing Jun proving that the noise he generated did not cause harm to Jiang Jianbo, even if Jiang Jianbo had not yet shown obvious symptoms, the fact that his life was disturbed by noise and he suffered mental harm was objectively existing. The second instance court, taking into account the time of noise generated by Jing Jun's steel processing, the distance between the two parties, and the volume of the noise, reasonably exercised its discretion in ordering Jing Jun to pay Jiang Jianbo RMB 2,000 in moral damages.

Case 8

China Environmental Protection Federation v. Wuxi Lihu Huishan Scenic Area Management Committee — Dispute over Compensation for Eco-environmental Damage

(1) Basic Facts

During the development and construction of the zoological and botanical garden and children's playground projects, the Wuxi Lihu Huishan Scenic Area Management Committee (hereinafter referred to as the Scenic Area Management Committee) unlawfully occupied approximately 20,000 square meters of forest land. The project involved a 2,500-square-meter exposed rocky slope area, which was a remnant from quarrying activities in the 1980s. The Scenic Area Management Committee did not conduct any construction on this plot. The China Environmental Protection Federation filed a lawsuit, requesting a judgment ordering the Scenic Area Management Committee to restore the unlawfully occupied forest land to its original use and compensate for losses, and immediately carry out re-greening and soil stabilization on the exposed land within the project area.

(2) Judgment

The Binhu District People's Court of Wuxi held at first instance that it was true that the Scenic Area Management Committee occupied 17,477 square meters of forest land without approval. However, the zoological and botanical garden project was part of the urban green space system, and the Scenic Area Management Committee later restored and added a certain amount of forest land, resulting in no significant damage. During the trial, the Scenic Area Management Committee had already paid vegetation restoration fees of over RMB 1.14 million, which should be deemed as having compensated for the ecological damage. The Scenic Area Management Committee unlawfully changed the use of 3,677 square meters of forest land and should restore it to its original condition. Given that the construction on this plot had been included in the project planning scope, and the project's sightseeing elevator had the function of serving as an escape and emergency access route, involving significant public interest, it was not feasible to restore it to its original condition. During the trial, the Scenic Area Management Committee proposed an off-site replanting plan, which was recognized by the competent authority and the China Environmental Protection Federation. After consulting with relevant professional institutions, a plan for off-site ecological restoration through replanting at Yangwan was determined. The Scenic Area Management Committee and other entities, as users of the exposed rocky slope area, had the obligation to continuously improve the condition of the area and eliminate the risk of further soil erosion. During the trial, the Scenic Area Management Committee voluntarily proposed a feasible re-greening plan, which the court confirmed and approved. The first instance court rendered a judgment in December 2012, ordering the Scenic Area Management Committee to complete the application procedures for changing the use of 17,477 square meters of forest land within one month, remit the off-site replanting costs of RMB 794,400 to a designated account, and complete the 4,500 square meters of off-site replanting at the Yangwan plot within six months, and the Scenic Area Management Committee and other land users to complete the re-greening and soil stabilization of the 2,500-square-meter exposed rocky slope area within six months.

(3) Typical Significance

The construction entity, the Scenic Area Management Committee, occupied and changed the use of forest land without approval during construction, causing damage to the ecological environment. It should bear civil liability for restoring the ecological environment. The particularity of this case lies in the fact that the land occupied by the project had been included in the project planning scope, and the project played an important role in the overall project, involving public interest, making direct restoration to the original condition infeasible. Under these circumstances, the first instance court, after consulting with professional institutions, adopted the off-site replanting plan for ecological restoration, exploring the methods for environmental polluters and ecological destroyers to bear civil liability. This avoided wasting social resources and restored the ecological capacity level within the entire region, providing a reference.

Case 9

Wang Shilong v. Liu Junbo — Dispute over Mining Right Transfer Contract

(1) Basic Facts

On August 27, 2007, Wang Shilong, in the name of Xinglong County Longsimin Marble Factory, entered into a mine transfer contract with Liu Junbo. The contract stipulated that Wang Shilong would transfer the Xinglong County Longsimin Marble Factory to Liu Junbo for a price of RMB 3.05 million. The contract also contained provisions on payment deadlines, liability for breach, and other matters. After the contract was signed, Liu Junbo paid a total of RMB 1.335 million in transfer fees and other amounts. Liu Junbo built a mine road and some factory buildings but did not mine the marble mine. Later, Wang Shilong filed a lawsuit on the grounds that Liu Junbo had not paid the full amount, requesting a judgment dissolving the mine transfer contract, ordering Liu Junbo to return the mine, and pay liquidated damages of RMB 760,000. Liu Junbo filed a counterclaim, requesting a judgment ordering Wang Shilong to continue performing the contract and compensate for losses of RMB 1.088 million.

(2) Judgment

The Chengde Intermediate People's Court dismissed both parties' claims at first instance. Both parties appealed to the Hebei High People's Court. The second instance court held that both Wang Shilong and Liu Junbo recognized that the subject matter of the transfer contract was the marble mine and the corresponding mining right. The mine transfer contract signed between the parties had been formed, but it was a contract that required approval from the relevant authorities according to law to become effective. Because the contract's provisions on the handover of mine procedures and other matters were unclear, both parties were responsible for the failure to perform the contract. For contracts that require approval or registration to become effective according to laws and administrative regulations, both parties should actively perform their respective obligations to promote the contract's effectiveness, in order to protect the legitimate rights and interests of all parties to the transaction. The second instance court rendered a judgment in February 2011, ordering Wang Shilong and Liu Junbo to submit relevant materials to the authorities in accordance with their respective obligations and apply for the approval procedures for the transfer of the Xinglong County Longsimin Marble Mine. Wang Shilong still disagreed and applied to the Supreme People's Court for retrial. The Supreme People's Court ruled to reject the retrial application.

(3) Typical Significance

Mineral resources are an important material foundation for human survival and sustainable economic and social development. The approval of mining right transfers is an important system for the state to regulate the orderly transfer of mining rights and achieve scientific protection and rational development of mineral resources. Where a mining right transfer has not been approved, the transfer contract has not yet taken legal effect. During the trial of this case, the second instance court strictly followed the legal provisions, held that the transfer contract had not taken effect due to lack of approval, and ordered both parties to handle the approval procedures for the mining right transfer in accordance with their respective obligations, actively promoting the contract's effectiveness. This safeguarded the order of the mining rights market transaction and also conformed to the principle of the Contract Law encouraging transactions and creating wealth.
